approach: Root cause: `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:297) puts CHANGELOG.md and the `changelog` default into every change reading, but the default is only a rule the producer must remember. No code compares the candidate's changed files with that deliverable before the verifier. The one existing check, `unchanged_planned_files` (run/mod.rs:1579, called at producer.rs:418), excuses any file that has a non-blank reason, and doc-only design jobs give one. So jobs 20261108-183842-fsaz and 20261028-000831-rkv5 were failed only by the final verdict. Fix, in three parts that share one predicate. (1) reading.rs: `changelog_unproduced(reading, changed)` beside `ensure_changelog`, sharing `CHANGELOG_PATH`. admission.rs wraps it in `changelog_required(git, base, reading, changed)`, which also skips the rule when the base classifies CHANGELOG.md as other than Governed. (2) Admission rule (the backstop the reading asks for): `admit_without_secrets` raises a `changelog` PolicyViolation naming CHANGELOG.md. Both `admit` callers (run/candidate.rs:154, run/mod.rs:773) close the job before the verifier. (3) Repair round: in `producer_loop` (producer.rs), beside `outside` and `gate`, the same `changelog_required` runs on the work tree after each report, with `&ctx.prediction` as the base (the user's repository commit that `unreconciled_in_snapshot` at producer.rs:428 and `candidate_stage` also use; the snapshot's own `base()` belongs to its isolated repository and is never passed to `self.git`). A missing changelog joins `problems`, the break condition and the send-back brief, and gets the extra send-back slot that `outside` has. Shared test doubles (fake producer, CLI `Scenario`) edit CHANGELOG.md when the brief lists it, because criterion 4 requires updated fixtures. CHANGELOG entry names the cause, the rule, the intended higher refusal rate and two transition consequences (retry from base; a resumed pre-upgrade candidate without a changelog entry is refused).

decisions.choice: Predicate `changelog_unproduced` in reading.rs, classification wrapper `changelog_required` in admission.rs (`pub(crate)`). Both the admission rule and the producer loop call the wrapper, so they cannot disagree. The wrapper is true only for capability `change`, a CHANGELOG.md deliverable with action Modify, a `changelog` default, no changed path equal to CHANGELOG.md (a leading `./` trimmed), and a Governed class for CHANGELOG.md at the base (`unwrap_or(PathClass::Governed)` as admission.rs:694 does).
decisions.reason: Admission is the first code that sees the reading and the change list together. `admit_without_secrets` (admission.rs:687, classify call at :691) is the existing seam that needs no gitleaks. Sharing `CHANGELOG_PATH` (reading.rs:293) with the code that adds the default stops the two drifting. The Governed skip is needed because `admit_without_secrets` already raises `owner-maintained` or `owner-private` for an edit to a readonly or excluded CHANGELOG.md (admission.rs:694-709); requiring the edit as well would make every change job in such a repository unadmittable.

decisions.choice: Add a producer-loop check beside `outside` and `gate` (producer.rs:420-431), after `changed` is computed (producer.rs:414): `let changelog_missing = !changes.is_empty() && crate::admission::changelog_required(&self.git, &ctx.prediction, ctx.reading, &changed)?;`. The base is `ctx.prediction`, the same value `producer_snapshot` uses as `p` (producer.rs:127) and `unreconciled_in_snapshot` receives (producer.rs:428). When true: remove CHANGELOG.md from `unchanged` (only matters when the producer gave no reason; a stated reason already removes it inside `unchanged_planned_files`, so in the main root-cause case the filter changes nothing and the file is named once by the new problem), add `&& !changelog_missing` to the break condition (446-452), push a problem after the `outside` block (not into `report_problems`), and append a section to the send-back brief through a new `append_missing_changelog` in send_back.rs (same style as `append_mirror_drift`, send_back.rs:226). The section names CHANGELOG.md, says the changelog default applies, and says a reason in unchanged_planned_files does not excuse it. `scope_slot_free` (producer.rs:519) becomes `(!outside.is_empty() || changelog_missing) && scope_send_backs < SCOPE_SEND_BACKS`; the doc comment of `SCOPE_SEND_BACKS` (run/mod.rs:1598) says so. At the limit the loop prints a line saying the job ends at admission.
decisions.reason: Answers the earlier finding that admission-only refusal turns a retryable verifier rejection into a Failed job that restarts from the base (`qualifies_for_tree_retry`, reading/retry.rs:330-346, needs state Rejected and no violations). The producer loop already checks the work tree against refusals the candidate stage would apply (`gate`, `outside`) and sends the producer back first. Both introspections propose a repair round. Using `ctx.prediction` (finding 8) gives `classify` a commit that exists in the user's repository; the snapshot's base commit exists only in its throwaway repository (athena-git snapshot.rs:3-6, 90), so passing it to `self.git` would error and fail every change job lacking CHANGELOG.md.

risks.mitigation: The producer loop sends the producer back first, with the extra slot, so admission refuses only a producer that ignored two send-backs. The refusal reason names CHANGELOG.md and fires before any verifier cost. The CHANGELOG entry states the consequence, and a run test pins it.

risks.risk: The producer-loop check is given the wrong base or repository and errors on every change job without a changelog edit.

risks.mitigation: Stated in the CHANGELOG entry. Admission test (f) shows an added CHANGELOG.md satisfies the rule. A repository that does not want this marks the file readonly or excluded, and the Governed skip then applies.

risks.risk: Existing tests with a change reading and a producer that edits only README.md or FAKE-CHANGE.md would be sent back or refused.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the rule and its predicate.
demonstrations.observes: `admit_without_secrets` pushes `violation("changelog", Some("CHANGELOG.md"), ..)` when `changelog_required` holds. `changelog_required` calls `reading::changelog_unproduced`, which is true only for capability `change`, a CHANGELOG.md Modify deliverable, a `changelog` default, and no changed path equal to CHANGELOG.md or ./CHANGELOG.md. The doc comments of the rule, `changelog_required` and the predicate name the root cause: the default was a rule the producer must remember, and no code compared the diff with the deliverables.

demonstrations.method: New admission tests drive `admit_without_secrets` through a helper `admit_files_with(reading, base_extra, files)`. The existing `admit_files` (admission.rs:1550) calls it with `&reading()` and no extra base files. Tests: (a) change reading with the `changelog` default and a CHANGELOG.md Modify deliverable, candidate only `docs/a.md`: exactly one violation, rule `changelog`, path CHANGELOG.md, detail containing CHANGELOG.md. (b) The same plus a CHANGELOG.md change: none. (c) A study reading with the default, and a change reading without it: none. (d) Base .gitattributes with `/CHANGELOG.md athena-readonly`: no `changelog` violation. (e) A reading with out_of_scope `the changelog` and the default still gets the violation (pins current behavior). (f) The base has no CHANGELOG.md and the candidate adds it (status added): none. Predicate unit tests in reading.rs beside the `ensure_changelog` tests (~2174-2210): true for docs-only; false for CHANGELOG.md, ./CHANGELOG.md and an added CHANGELOG.md; true for docs/CHANGELOG.md; false for a study reading.
demonstrations.observes: (a) passes with one `changelog` violation; (b), (c), (d) and (f) find no `changelog` violation; (e) finds it. With the rule's call removed from `admit_without_secrets`, test (a) fails on its one-violation assertion.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `changelog` push removed from `admit_without_secrets`, test (a) fails on its one-violation assertion; with `changelog_unproduced` returning false, the reading.rs predicate tests fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `admit_without_secrets(&AdmissionInput)` (admission.rs:687), the function `admit` calls first; `admit` is not called because its secret scan needs gitleaks, and existing tests use the same seam (admission.rs:1550-1587, read). Fixture: a temp git repo and a `Reading` built in the test, injected through `AdmissionInput.reading`, `.changes`, `.candidate` and `.base`. `admit_without_secrets` and `admit_files` exist; the `admit_files_with` helper is added by plan step 3. The double builds only the repository and reading; the rule runs in production code.

demonstrations.method: Admission level (admission.rs): a docs-only design reading (class_of_work `docs`, capability `change`, deliverable docs/design/x.md modify) is passed through `crate::reading::ensure_changelog`, the path both failed jobs took. The test asserts the reading now lists CHANGELOG.md and the `changelog` default, then runs `admit_files_with` with candidate docs/design/x.md alone and asserts a `changelog` violation. Run level (run/tests.rs), three tests with the `Docs` capability given an `id` field set to "change" and a scripted reader returning capability `change` with deliverable README.md: (1) `a_change_job_sent_back_for_the_changelog_adds_it_and_reaches_the_verifier`: pass one edits README.md only and reports CHANGELOG.md in unchanged_planned_files with a reason; the second producer brief contains a `## Sent back` section naming CHANGELOG.md and saying a reason does not excuse it; pass two also edits CHANGELOG.md; the invocations are Reader, Producer, Producer, Verifier. This test would also fail if the producer-loop check used the snapshot's base commit in the user's repository, so it pins finding 8. (2) `a_change_job_that_never_adds_the_changelog_is_refused_before_the_verifier`: the producer omits it on every pass; there are three producer invocations (shared slot plus the extra slot); no Verifier invocation; the outcome is Failed with a reason containing `admission refused the change` and `CHANGELOG.md`; the candidate holds a `changelog` violation; `qualifies_for_tree_retry` is false for it (pins the restart-from-base consequence). (3) `a_change_job_that_edits_the_changelog_at_once_reaches_the_verifier`: one producer invocation, then a Verifier invocation. Unit tests for `append_missing_changelog` in run_pin_tests.rs (flag false leaves the text unchanged; the section names CHANGELOG.md).
demonstrations.observes: Admission test: violation naming CHANGELOG.md for a reading built by `ensure_changelog`. Run level: (1) records a second producer brief naming CHANGELOG.md and then a Verifier; (2) ends Failed at admission with no Verifier; (3) reaches the verifier with one producer run.

demonstrations.observes: A new first item under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Changed` names the cause (the default was a rule the producer must remember and no code compared the diff with the deliverables; jobs 20261108-183842-fsaz and 20261028-000831-rkv5). It names the `changelog` admission rule, `changelog_unproduced`, the producer-loop send-back, the Governed-only skip, and the updated test doubles. It states that the higher refusal rate is intended (about 5% of change jobs, an estimate), that a repository without CHANGELOG.md must now have every change job create it, that a job refused at admission restarts from the base on retry, and that a resumed pre-upgrade candidate without a changelog entry is refused. The existing tests that `include_str!` CHANGELOG.md still pass.
